text:
Jordan (People Ops): Heads up — I'm seeing three managers report that review forms locked after 11:59p PST even though we approved deadline extensions earlier today. Need quick guidance on safe unlocks + audit trail. cc @Marta (HR Ops)
Marta (HR Ops): Ugh, thanks. Are these extensions via the 'extension requests' form (LOA/medical) or ad-hoc manager approvals? Example thread pls.
Priya G (Eng Manager): This is mine — two ICs had medical LOA approvals (sent at 09:12) and I added the extension flag, but their forms are closed and reviewers can't submit. The UI "reopen" button is greyed out.
Ethan R (IC): Confirmed — tried to re-save a reply and got "submission window closed". I can still view comments but not submit.
Marta (HR Ops): Ok — that matches a timing edge case where the lock step ran before our manual flags propagated to the form service. We have a safe unblock path but need to ensure auditability.
Jordan (People Ops): What do you need from managers? CSV? timestamps?
Marta (HR Ops): Please supply a CSV with: email, reviewer_email (if applicable), form_id, approved_extension_reason (short), approved_by, approval_ts. Small sample header:
```
email,reviewer_email,form_id,approved_extension_reason,approved_by,approval_ts
alice@example.com,eve@example.com,form_9801,medical LOA,Priya G,2026-03-20T09:12:00Z
```
Marta (HR Ops): Once we have that, ops will run a controlled unlock job that: 1) reopens the specific forms, 2) writes an immutable audit entry, 3) tags the submission with the extension reason so analytics/queries can exclude them from on-time metrics.
Jordan (People Ops): ETA on job run? Any risk of duplicate submissions/overrides?
Marta (HR Ops): We'll run within the hour after CSV receipt. The job tombstones the original closed event and creates a new "reopen-for-extension" event id; duplicates are guarded by idempotency keys. Managers should tell reviewers to NOT re-upload attachments until we confirm.
Priya G (Eng Manager): Sending CSV now. One more question — what about manager handback deadlines? If the reviewer submits late, will that cascade?
Marta (HR Ops): Good q — reopened submissions keep their original reviewer roles and timestamps are marked. For scoring/sla, we'll apply a flag so calibration chairs see "extension-applied" and exclude from strict on-time counts. Calibration window still expects managerial handbacks within 72h after reopen; mention exceptions in the calibration packet.
review-bot: System notice: review forms locked due to deadline enforcement at 2026-03-20T08:00:00Z. Automated unlock requests require People Ops approval.
Jordan (People Ops): Thanks all. Once Marta confirms job complete, I'll post the list back into the manager tracker and ping reviewers to submit.
Marta (HR Ops): Job complete — reopened 2 forms from Priya's CSV. Audit IDs: REOPEN-8842, REOPEN-8843. I've added the extension flag to both records.
Priya G (Eng Manager): Got it — told reviewers to submit now. Thanks! :thumbsup:
Ethan R (IC): Submitted successfully. Forms looked unchanged except for the extension flag note.
Jordan (People Ops): Closing loop: I'll add a short FAQ blurb about this edge case and the CSV unlock flow so managers can self-serve next cycle. Will share draft here for quick review.
Marta (HR Ops): Please include the 'do not re-upload attachments' line and the exact CSV header. Also add the audit ID examples.
Priya G (Eng Manager): Happy to review the FAQ. Quick note: can we add a tiny UI hint next cycle when an extension is applied? Saves a lot of slack pings.
Marta (HR Ops): Agree — filing a small product request ticket.
Jordan (People Ops): Perfect. Closing thread — thanks everyone.
